title: t1: last token picks a position, MLP looks up (last token, token there)
label: verified
behavior: BOS + 6 tokens from {ge, gu, lu, sa, vi, zo}; the model outputs one symbol at the last position. local-full checkpoint benchmarks/glassbox-bench/seed-2/tasks/t1/model.pt (2 layers, 3 heads per layer, full precision).
summary: The output depends on exactly two input tokens: the last token (position 6) and one earlier token whose position is chosen by the last token alone (ge->5, sa->5, gu->1, vi->2, lu->3, zo->4). The answer is a fixed 6x6 lookup g(last token, pointed token). Head 1.2 is the pointer (one-hot attention from position 6), mlp1 computes the lookup, and mlp0 is also required. Heads 0.0, 0.1, 0.2, 1.0 and 1.1 are inert. All numbers are from the local-full (full precision) backend. On 400 held-out inputs the algorithm agrees with the model 400/400; ablating the circuit drops accuracy to 0.245, ablating everything else leaves it at 1.0.
pseudocode:
ids: 2=ge 3=gu 4=lu 5=sa 6=vi 7=zo; x[1..6] = input tokens
last = x[6]
ptr  = {ge:5, sa:5, gu:1, vi:2, lu:3, zo:4}[last]        # head 1.2
b    = x[ptr]
out  = g[last][b]                                          # mlp1

g (rows = last, cols = b in order ge gu lu sa vi zo):
 ge: ge sa vi sa ge ge
 gu: sa vi gu lu ge zo
 lu: vi gu ge sa gu ge
 sa: lu zo vi sa ge vi
 vi: zo lu gu zo ge gu
 zo: lu vi lu gu sa ge

claims.text: The model performs a deterministic behaviour (clean accuracy 1.0 on 200 inputs).
Head 1.2 attends one-hot from the last position to a position set by the last token alone: gu->1, vi->2, lu->3, zo->4, ge and sa->5 (attention 1.0 in every case, 12 prompts each).
Head 1.2 is necessary: mean-ablating it leaves 0.109 of the clean metric.
mlp0 and mlp1 are necessary: mean-ablating either leaves under 0.02 of the clean metric.
Heads 0.0, 0.1, 0.2, 1.0 and 1.1 play no part: joint mean ablation leaves the metric at 1.0, and the circuit {mlp0, 1.2, mlp1} alone keeps accuracy 1.0.

The output is the lookup g(last token, token at the pointed position); this algorithm matches the model on 400/400 held-out inputs (null agreement p95 = 0.213). An earlier version with one misread table entry (gu,ge) scored 195/200 and was corrected.

limitations: The lookup table g and the pointer map were read off the model's input/output pairs (E0001, E0007) and then tested; I found no simpler closed-form rule for g, so it is reported as a 36-entry table.

The exact role of mlp0 was not isolated (whether it feeds the query, the key or the value of head 1.2, or mlp1 directly). A path-patching attempt with mlp0 as sender errored (unsupported sender) and was not replaced.
The first verification (V0001) had one wrong table entry from a transcription error; it is corrected in V0002. The pointer rule and circuit were unchanged.
Attention tests used 12 prompts per last-token group; the held-out agreement (400/400) is the stronger test of the pointer rule.
open_questions: Is g a composition of simpler operations (e.g. a per-token map followed by arithmetic)? The gu row is a permutation but the others are not.
What does mlp0 compute, and at which positions is it needed?
